scope: Powerhouse One Loop / GitHub PR metadata / protected delivery
symptom: Required and BRAIN delivery evaluated stale pull_request event payload after the live PR body had been corrected, causing protected delivery to remain red even though the repository head and live PR metadata were valid.
root_causes: The first recovery merge changed the effective PR base from b573a31d0547979bf9c708e4f56da0fa27502688 to 5e9ae9f2633ffb1b0bdd07c2ba8b44b934d927b9 while the original workflow event still carried the old declared Base-SHA.
scripts/publish_approved_blog_v2.py was a legitimate changed path but was omitted from the declared Change-Scope, producing SCOPE_CONTAMINATED during Required preflight.
Editing the PR body does not create a fresh run for workflows that use the default pull_request activity types, and rerunning an existing workflow attempt reuses the original event payload.
fix: Updated the existing PR metadata in place with the exact current Base-SHA and the missing approved-blog publisher path, then created this canonical learning writeback on the same branch so GitHub emits a normal synchronize event whose payload contains the corrected metadata. No parallel branch, PR, queue or product-lineage was created.
prevention: When protected CI consumes github.event.pull_request.body, treat the event payload as immutable per workflow run and never assume a later live PR edit changes an existing attempt.
After an effective base change, update Base-SHA before requesting fresh protected checks.
Before expensive CI, compare changed paths with declared Change-Scope and report the first unexpected path exactly.
Use a legitimate same-lineage writeback/synchronize event rather than close-reopen or empty commits when a fresh PR event context is required.
terminal_acceptance: Remain RECOVERY_IN_PROGRESS until the new exact head has fresh Required and BRAIN delivery checks terminal green, is protected-merged with exact-head identity, and main/readback confirms the One Loop control-plane on protected main.
